record.paper_title: Hénon maps: a list of open problems
record.original_question: For a generalized Hénon map f, describe all generalized Hénon maps g such that the associated compact complex surfaces S̄(f) and S̄(g) are biholomorphic.

evidence.quote: Question 42. — Let f be any generalized Hénon map. Describe the set of all generalized Hénon maps g such that S¯(f) is biholomorphic to S¯(g).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A generalized Hénon map is a polynomial automorphism of $\mathbb{C}^2$ of the form
$$f = f_1 \circ f_2 \circ \cdots \circ f_n,$$
where each $f_i(x,y) = (y,\, p_i(y) - a_i x)$ with $p_i \in \mathbb{C}[y]$ a polynomial of degree $d_i \geq 2$ and $a_i \in \mathbb{C}^*$. To such a map $f$ one associates a compact complex surface $\overline{S}(f)$ obtained by compactifying $\mathbb{C}^2$ along the line at infinity, performing the canonical sequence of blow-ups that resolve the indeterminacies of $f$ at infinity, and then taking the quotient of a neighborhood of the resulting exceptional divisor at infinity by the action induced by $f$ (so that $\overline{S}(f)$ is a minimal compact complex surface, in fact a Kato surface, naturally attached to the germ of $f$ at infinity).

Problem. Given a generalized Hénon map $f$, describe explicitly the set of all generalized Hénon maps $g$ such that the associated compact complex surfaces $\overline{S}(f)$ and $\overline{S}(g)$ are biholomorphic.
artifact.status_search_result: A 2024 preprint by F. Bacher ("Hénon maps with biholomorphic Kato surfaces", arXiv:2410.19547) proves that the Kato surfaces associated to two generalized Hénon maps are biholomorphic if and only if the maps are affinely conjugate in $\mathrm{Aut}(\mathbb{C}^2)$, thereby answering the classification question.

status_evidence.title: Hénon maps with biholomorphic Kato surfaces
status_evidence.snippet: The Kato surfaces associated to germs of generalized Hénon maps near infinity are biholomorphic if and only if the maps are conjugate in Aut(C^2); two generalized Hénon maps are conjugate near infinity iff they are affinely conjugate.
status_evidence.claim: Provides a complete classification: biholomorphism of the associated Kato surfaces is equivalent to affine conjugacy of the generalized Hénon maps.
